name: Identixweb Limited
sector: Software products / Shopify merchant apps and accounting SaaS; bespoke IT services
research_status: Deep v3.0 research; evidence holds, not incomplete placeholder
identity_status: Verified exact legal issuer and security
summary:
Identixweb has a real, profitable merchant-app business, not merely SaaS branding. Its standalone revenue grew from ₹3.0154 crore in FY21 to ₹11.0868 crore in FY26, a 29.75% five-year CAGR. Consolidated FY26 revenue was ₹13.0474 crore, up 43.49%. But recurring-contract potential is not the same as verified recurring-revenue quality: paid merchants, retention, churn, ARR and cohort returns are undisclosed in the reviewed material.

The central investment issue is the cash cost of building the next products. FY26 newly capitalized development was ₹11.1612 crore versus operating EBITDA ₹7.4990 crore. CFO ₹3.9024 crore less cash capex ₹11.2535 crore gives FCF−₹7.3511 crore. Software can be highly capital efficient; here attributable returns on those additional development rupees are not yet demonstrated. Accounting bridges and current funding are also unresolved, so CAP, CASH, BAL, R and L remain NS rather than guessed neutral or low scores.

At a stale secondary 1 October close of ₹65, market capitalization is ₹67.8701 crore. No ordinary target, entry price or expected return is supported. BQS, GQS and IAS are all NS, with exact missing-factor bounds disclosed separately. Classification: Hold — unresolved, not an evidence-backed compounder. The decisive next evidence is paid-cohort economics, an auditor-backed cash reconciliation and current funding, not a lower headline P/E.

G1 is Conditional: no substantiated severe diversion found, but compliance and subsidiary allocation merit monitoring. G2 is Hold — unresolved for EPS/CFO/tax/capital-addition bridges. sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH NS, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 4, L NS. Every scored point has material facts, a contrary fact and cited evidence; missing critical inputs remain null. REV uses the five-year constant-issuer window chosen before scoring, not the faster consolidated/acquired window. It starts 8 in the 20–30% band with no discretionary adjustment.

BQS weights are 20/20/12/10/12/10/8/8% across GOV/MOAT/REV/DUR/CAP/CASH/BAL/EXEC. Known contribution 3.96 covers 70%; exact unresolved-factor bounds 4.26–6.96. GQS is Growth Quality, not governance: REV 40%, DUR 20%, EARN 15%, CAP 15%, CASH 10%. Known contribution 5.15 covers 75%, with bounds 5.40–7.65. IAS uses Q(BQS)25%, R 35%, D 20%, P 10%, L 10%; known contribution 1.00 covers 30%, direct bounds 1.70–8.00 and BQS-propagated bounds 2.515–7.240. All three aggregate points remain NS; known contributions are not renormalized scores or rankings.

No numerical governance, funding or poor-cash override is applied because no evidenced G1/G3 failure or CAP/CASH≤3 point has been established. G2/G4 still block favorable new-investment classification. A±1 change in GOV or MOAT moves the partial BQS contribution 0.20; REV moves BQS 0.12 and GQS 0.40, but none repairs missing evidence. Bounds are mathematical, not confidence intervals or return probabilities.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The parent develops Shopify apps such as iCart and delivery/payment/shipping tools and also provides bespoke web/software services. Apps are distributed through a third-party commerce platform; merchant demand, store survival, product usefulness, discoverability, reviews and platform policies determine economics. The contractual opportunity can be recurring, but reported sales mix is not a separately audited subscription ARR ledger. Usage claims include 14000+ global merchants, not a verified count of currently paying accounts. Free installs, trials, active users and retained paid customers cannot be equated.

Munim ERP is an accounting/GST software subsidiary. At 31 March 2026 it was 50.01% owned; FY26 revenue ₹1.9606 crore and loss ₹1.3103 crore compare with ₹0.5593 crore revenue in FY25. Consolidation adds its full sales and cash costs, while owners are entitled only to their residual claim after NCI and any intercompany financing. The proposed June loan conversion raises ownership to 70.05% without creating new group cash. The US LLC was inactive/unfunded in the reviewed reporting, so it receives no positive model value.

The useful operating dashboard would split app subscription/usage revenue, bespoke services and Munim; paid logo and revenue retention, installs-to-paid conversion, ARPA, platform take-rate, churn causes, CAC by channel, support cost and developer cash spend. None is inferred from the SaaS label. There is no manufactured inventory or factory-capacity requirement to penalize. The economic capacity constraint is successful engineering, distribution and support.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Potential advantages are merchant workflow integration, a functioning portfolio, app-store presence and accumulated technical/support experience. A useful cart or delivery tool can earn recurring fees and become sticky in a store’s workflow. But low physical capital does not itself prove low replacement effort or pricing power. Competing apps, merchant switching, Shopify-native functionality, search rankings and platform access can dilute those advantages. The prospectus identifies Shopify as 85.41% of FY24 standalone revenue and 58.98% in H1 FY25; top-three counterparties contributed 93.31% and 83.76%. This is a platform/collection concentration measure, not proof of only one ultimate merchant.

The peer frame deliberately avoids false precision. Tally is an accounting/GST workflow incumbent and ClearTax offers GST/enterprise compliance tools, making both relevant to Munim’s functional competition. Their private-company retention, current margins and market values are not invented. Intellect Design Arena supplies enterprise financial software and is a listed software-product capital-allocation comparator, but its regulated-bank clients, implementation cycles and scale differ materially from low-ticket Shopify merchant apps. It is not used to justify an automatic valuation premium or a peer P/E median. These three official-source comparators show that software branding alone is not a moat.

MOAT 5 reflects differentiated niche capability but no verified durable pricing or retention advantage. The disconfirming test is whether old paid cohorts keep paying after platform/promotion changes without escalating acquisition/support costs. Strong net retention with low CAC payback could support a higher score; user-count growth without cohort cash returns would not.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The five-year comparable parent series is FY21 ₹3.0154079 crore, FY22 ₹6.0009, FY23 ₹6.2211, FY24 ₹6.3290, FY25 ₹8.5338 and FY26 ₹11.0868. The FY21 anchor is visually verified in the original annual-report financial highlights; the same issuer perimeter avoids Munim acquisition distortion. CAGR 29.7454% over five actual intervals and 21.2401% from FY23–26 both map to REV 8, with no current-trajectory adjustment. Ten-year CAGR is unavailable: incorporation in 2017 means eleven comparable annual observations do not exist.

Reported consolidated revenues FY22–26 are ₹6.0009/6.2211/6.3336/9.0931/13.0474 crore, but FY22 is standalone and FY23 includes associate accounting, with Munim control acquired in February 2024. The consolidated FY23–26 CAGR 28.0026% is shown for context, not relabeled organic. FY26 parent sales addition ₹2.5530 crore and Munim addition ₹1.4013 crore reconcile the ₹3.9543 crore group increase. Parent growth 29.9163% is materially below consolidated 43.4868%, yet still strong.

H1 FY26 revenue ₹5.7844 crore versus ₹4.7105 is 22.7980% higher; H2 balancing revenue ₹7.2630 versus ₹4.3827 is 65.7198% higher. These are half-years, not quarterly observations. Latest comparable TTM is FY26; unavailable H1 FY27 is not estimated. FY23–24’s flat parent revenue is important contrary evidence against projecting uninterrupted exponential growth. Price, FX, app mix and ultimate paid volume cannot be fully decomposed; no TAM estimate substitutes for actual sales.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Reinvestment is principally people and product development, not factories. FY25 new capitalized development ₹4.5642 crore removes an internal transfer of ₹0.7858 crore from gross intangible additions to avoid double counting. FY26 new development ₹11.1612 crore consists of parent ₹6.2799 crore and Munim ₹4.8813 crore. Parent development-in-progress reached ₹11.4997 crore with no amortization before commercialization, while Munim net intangibles reached ₹8.1530 crore. Auditor focus on AS26 capitalization is appropriate: feasibility, useful life, future benefit and salary attribution require judgment. Legitimate growth capitalization can still absorb much more cash than reported profit suggests.

Expensing all new development and reversing related amortization once is a deliberately severe cash-cost diagnostic, not a claim that all R&D should legally be expensed. It takes FY25 operating EBIT to approximately ₹0.5748 crore and FY26 to−₹4.3442 crore before any assumed loss-tax credit. Some development may generate future income and some may be maintenance/replacement effort; the split is undisclosed. Scenarios vary development spend±25% and normalize mature cash-cost EBITDA instead of valuing inflated reported-style margins.

Three-year book incremental NOPAT/IC is about 15.286%, with numerator ₹3.321975 crore and denominator ₹21.7318 crore; the 13–18% post-tax nominal capital-cost range is illustrative. Acquisition/perimeter change, IPO cash, uncommissioned software, NCI and capitalization contaminate this proxy. Five-year attributable capital returns and cohort economics are absent, so CAP remains NS. A small physical asset base is not a penalty, but a growing intangible balance is not evidence of high incremental returns either. The runway becomes investable only when paid adoption and retained cash margins repay new-product investment.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The promoter group held 62.99% at 31 March 2026. Managerial remuneration was ₹45 lakh versus ₹58.89 lakh the previous year; relative salary ₹12 lakh is separately disclosed. Related-party transactions are described by the company as in the ordinary course and arm’s-length. That response is preserved, not overridden by an assumption that every family or subsidiary transaction is abusive. Subsidiary advances without specified repayment schedules nevertheless make capital-allocation discipline and minority economics material.

The May 8 postal notice proposed service transactions up to ₹10 crore and financial support/loans up to ₹20 crore. June 10 voting and scrutinizer results confirm both resolutions passed. One summary date says 2025, but the covering letter, notice and substantive report consistently identify 2026; this clerical inconsistency is not treated as a missing vote or fraud. June 24 board approval to convert ₹12.2348 crore old subsidiary loan into 6693 shares, targeting 70.05% ownership, is separate. Its stated 30-day completion expectation is not proof of completed allotment. The conversion is noncash group restructuring, not fresh funding.

Audit history requires context: the earlier auditor’s June 2024 resignation cited preoccupation; a casual-vacancy and subsequent one-year appointment followed, then A.K.Ostwal was appointed 27 September 2025 for five years to 2030. These changes are not by themselves misconduct. Reports are unmodified. Repeated late ROC forms are explained as clerical omission and stated as rectified with additional fees and preventive measures; recurrence still weakens controls. No substantiated severe diversion or material adverse court order was located in reviewed filings. Execution shows launched products and growth, but no app-level cash-return scorecard or proven Munim profitability. GOV 5 and EXEC 5 preserve that mixed record.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The history uses consolidated group PAT against consolidated CFO and parent-attributable PAT for equity EPS. FY24–26 summed reported CFO ₹10.5421 crore divided by group PAT ₹10.5917 crore is 0.995317, not an average of annual ratios. Cash capex ₹23.6739 crore produces cumulative FCF−₹13.1318 crore. Capex belongs to investing cash flow; it explains cash after reinvestment, not a missing operating-cash item. No lease liability is invented from AS-format rent expenses. Gross profit, contract assets and maintenance/growth development split are ND where not separately reliable.

The FY24 prospectus-versus-later PAT difference ₹0.1301 crore is explained at category level by additional gratuity ₹0.1341 less deferred-tax benefit ₹0.0040; CFO is unchanged because the provision addback rose. This is retained as a resolved comparison explanation, not a forensic accusation. Other bridges remain open. FY25 reported EPS 4.52 uses roughly group PAT, whereas parent PAT ₹3.7198 crore over 7361550 shares is 5.0530. FY26 owner EPS 5.1274 (reported 5.13) over 10441550 shares gives only 1.4721% comparable per-share growth, not the 13.5% implied by 5.13/4.52. IPO share expansion is 41.8390%, original-holder dilution 29.4975%; the earlier 94:1 bonus alone is not dilution.

CFO starts from full group PBT but adjusts minority attribution +₹0.3931 crore FY25 and−₹0.6550 FY26. Why ownership attribution changes group cash is unresolved. FY26 tax-paid line ₹2.1901 crore equals net P&L tax, not current tax ₹2.2570, while provisions contain tax-payable movements. Pure removal of minority lines yields a sensitivity, not corrected audited cash. Gross additions ₹11.7033 crore versus cash capex ₹11.2535 leave ₹0.4498 crore requiring a noncash/capital-creditor bridge. May results versus annual report also reclassify ₹0.2788 crore between advances and other current assets without changing totals; this is not an asset disappearance, but other cash-flow labels still need reconciliation.

March cash ₹9.2999 crore is not all free: ₹1.9550 crore IPO marketing is earmarked, tax payable ₹2.0557 crore, gratuity ₹0.4653 and debt ₹0.1115 must be considered once. ₹5.508 crore IPO application money was already in FY25 cash; FY26 net cash equity inflow ₹9.3193 is not added again. Net issue-object versus equity bridge differs ₹0.0095 crore; prepaid issue costs ₹0.1955 are not charged twice. Already-paid advances are not new future funding outflows or automatic releases. Receivables fell from ₹2.6228 to ₹1.6421 crore, with FY26 balances under six months versus prior six-to-twelve-month classification; average-balance revenue-proxy days remain about 59.65. No full cash conversion cycle is manufactured without compatible purchases/payables data. These unresolved cash and ownership bridges justify G2 Hold and CASH NS, without asserting fraud.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The stale ₹65 quote and current 10441550 shares give equity value ₹67.870075 crore. FY26 parent-PAT P/E is 12.68×; using group PAT gives 14.44× and standalone PAT about 11.29×, demonstrating why claim perimeter matters. Parent book value excludes negative NCI. A consolidated EV is left NS because current deployable cash and fair NCI claims are unverified; negative minority book equity is not a free cash adjustment. The full-development-expensed operating diagnostic is loss-making, so a simple low P/E is not an adequate cash-earnings valuation.

Annual cash scenarios separately model parent apps/services and Munim. Growth, reported-style operating margins, development cash, tangible capex, taxes and receivable investment are explicit assumptions, not guidance. March cash is rolled through 202 pre-entrydays, then 163 days to FY27 end, FY28–31, and 202/366 days of FY32 only. October 2031 terminal LTM uses 163/365 of FY31 plus 202/366 of FY32; later cash gaps do not govern the horizon. Required reserves are retained and signed cash deficits are not clipped away. Opening taxes/debt/capital-creditor sensitivity are checked immediately; floor step-ups are checked at every segment start and end. Period-end rescue ledgers represent funds assumed available just in time during a negative linear cash path, not permission to run below the floor until year-end.

Base parent growth starts 20% then decelerates to 12%, with Munim 60% decelerating to 20%; reported-style margins and real development spend are separate. The illustrative 12× exit applies to cash-cost EBITDA after recurring development, not capitalized accounting EBITDA. Parent transfers fund subsidiary needs as new interest-free intercompany support, which cancels group cash; terminal recovery is capped at recoverable subsidiary value, residual ownership/NCI is applied once. Old loan conversion is conditional and does not create cash. Required cash and outstanding claims are not added twice; no operational office or software book asset is valued again on top of operating EV.

No-rescue peak gaps are about ₹22.8860/6.6689/3.0931 crore in bear/base/bull. Every no-rescue return is null after a cash-floor breach, and all ordinary IRRs/entry prices remain null because current funding is not verified. A separate hypothetical rescue at ₹32.50 per share, 3% fees, yields IRRs−29.38%/13.47%/36.76%, with gross/net proceeds, share expansion and holder dilution shown separately. These are not accessible financing offers or expected returns. Hurdle sensitivities 12/15/18%, issue discounts 25/50/70%, fees 0/3/6%, development±25%, margins−10 pp, receivables+10% of sales, opening cash−₹2 crore, launch delay and exit 8/12/16× are explicit. At 15% and no dividends the ₹65 entry needs ₹130.74 terminal per share; a 12× parent-only no-cash/no-dilution algebra requires roughly ₹11.38 crore terminal cash EBITDA, versus about ₹1.5212 crore FY26 parent EBITDA less new development, not a target. P 4 assesses these price-implied expectations: development normalization, growth, profitable product adoption and financing terms must jointly hold. Even the base rescue fee/discount grid returns only 10.90–14.87%, not a conservative margin over the 15% hurdle. This is separate from generic business predictability and does not convert R from NS.

No DCF is forced: unverified cohorts, current funding, development useful lives and mature cash margins make a terminal perpetuity falsely precise. Terminal-value share is therefore not applicable/null, not 0%. Peer descriptions are not a valuation multiple shortcut. No scenario-probability-weighted IRR is fabricated.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case does not require accounting fraud. Shopify distribution or monetization changes, merchant closures, app substitution or poor paid conversion can lower app cash contribution while engineers and marketing still cost money. Capitalized products may need write-downs or further spending; a high reported margin then overstates cash distributable to owners. Munim’s loss and negative net worth can demand additional parent support, and a loan-to-equity conversion changes the seniority of existing claims. Approval to lend is not outside cash.

A dated low-debt balance sheet offers protection, but not unlimited runway after a large development program. If actual October cash is below the March-rollforward assumptions, or taxes/advances/obligations are less favorable, dilution can begin before the hypothetical entry. Rescue at a deep discount transfers economics away from existing holders; fees consume proceeds separately. Cash gaps in this report are modeled risks, not allegations of actual unpaid liabilities or insolvency.

Liquidity compounds fundamental loss: a 2000-share lot, limited observed trades and unknown order-book depth can prevent an orderly ₹5 lakh-size exit at the displayed price. Product IP or office book values are not assumed liquidation proceeds. A bear rescue can still lose roughly 29% per year under this illustrative five-year path, and inability to finance at all could be worse. D 3 reflects plausible severe capital impairment despite a real incumbent parent business. Evidence that could falsify the bear case is sustained cohort retention, cash profitability after all development, verified funding and stronger paid adoption without ever-growing support costs.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold wealth in five years require 37.97% and 58.49% annualized per-share returns respectively. At the stale ₹65 reference, no dilution and 15× terminal owner P/E, 5× requires approximately ₹22.6234 crore parent-attributable annual profit and 10× ₹45.2467 crore, versus FY26 ₹5.3538 crore. These are reverse expectations, not forecasts; a lower exit multiple, rescue share issuance, tax/cash reinvestment or NCI claims raise the required operating outcome.

The growth route would need multiple durable paid app franchises and/or profitable Munim expansion, not only more installs or capitalized releases. Reinvestment must produce high incremental cash returns, retained cohorts and enough cash to fund growth; current CAP evidence is missing. In the bullish hypothetical rescue the terminal upside is substantial, but a financing assumption and cash-margin assumptions do much of the work. That is insufficient to label a 5× or 10× compounder.

Classification of the multibagger case is speculative/unsupported. Track actual paid product cohorts and fully diluted cash earnings before claiming asymmetric upside. A small starting market capitalization and an addressable global merchant market do not by themselves make a large per-share outcome likely.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
First, reconcile accounting before upgrading quality: obtain the FY25 owner EPS basis, group CFO minority adjustments, tax-paid/provisions reconciliation, asset additions versus cash capex and results-to-annual-report reclassifications. Treat the explained FY24 gratuity bridge separately from still-open items. A written issuer/auditor schedule with line-level cash movements would resolve more than a generic unmodified-opinion reminder.

Second, establish current financeability: dated bank cash and liens, IPO-object balances, post-March development/marketing spending, tax/gratuity obligations, capital creditors and availability/terms of any financing. Confirm the June subsidiary share allotment and actual resulting ownership, rather than assuming board approval equals completion. Track any new RPT advances and whether new funding is external to the group.

Third, build a software-specific operating dashboard: paying merchants by app, old/new cohort revenue, gross/net retention, churn, upgrades, ARPA, app-store ranking dependence, platform net take, CAC/payback, support cost and development maintenance versus growth cash. For Munim, seek paid subscribers, realized revenue, segment gross contribution and loss-to-cash-break-even progress. A launch without paying cash adoption is not the milestone.

Finally, before any proposed transaction verify the actual BSE quote, complete 20/60 session traded/no-print record, current lot, surveillance/lock-in/pledge changes, spread and depth. Invalidate the thesis if old cohorts deteriorate, capitalized development rises without monetization, subsidiary support grows without return, accounting bridges worsen or funding requires deeply dilutive rescue. Reassess after the next actual comparable filing; no invented quarterly schedule or automatic order is implied.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| Development cash productivity | FY26 new development ₹11.1612 cr versus groupEBITDA ₹7.4990 cr; full-expense EBIT diagnostic−₹4.3442 cr. | Product-by-product spend, commercialization and retained paid cash contribution; maintenance/growth split. | Next FY27 interim and each subsequent half-year. | Development spend remains above operating EBITDA without improving retained cash contribution. | Major abandoned/impaired products or sustained cash losses with no funded monetization path. |
| Munim loss and parent support | FY26 revenue ₹1.9606 cr, loss ₹1.3103 cr, net worth−₹3.1019 cr; March ownership 50.01%. | Paid subscriber revenue, cash loss and new support reconciled separately from old loan conversion. | Next subsidiary/parent financial disclosure; before any new material support transaction. | Loss/support rises above FY26 scale without attributable paid-revenue/contribution improvement. | Parent funds consumed without a credible funded break-even plan or minority claim reconciliation. |
| Owner EPS and group CFO bridges | FY25 owner EPS computed 5.0530 versus reported 4.52; FY26 CFO minority−₹0.6550 cr; additions/cash gap ₹0.4498 cr. | Auditor/issuer line-by-line EPS, minority, cash-tax, provisions and additions reconciliation. | Before any G2 upgrade; next financial results or by 30 November 2026 review. | Unresolved comparatives repeat or cash statements acquire further unexplained classification changes. | Verified material misstatement or unreconciled cash existence evidence, not a mere unexplained label. |

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification is Hold — unresolved, not Avoid — evidenced governance, not verified distress, and not an evidence-backed compounder. G1 is Conditional; G2/G3/G4 are Hold. BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS. The available operating record justifies continued research, while unresolved cash economics, current funding and tradability prevent a favorable investment action or cross-company ranking point. This distinction avoids both dismissing an asset-light software company as inherently weak and awarding SaaS quality on branding alone.

For a new position, the present evidence supports no executable entry recommendation. For an existing holding, the relevant work is position-specific liquidity and funding verification rather than assuming a stale close can be realized. No personalized position size is prescribed. The ₹5 lakh reference rounds down to 3 lots/6000 shares/₹3.90 lakh or up to 4 lots/8000 shares/₹5.20 lakh; the ceiling exceeds the illustration. At 2/5/10% participation, observed small-volume sessions often allow zero whole lots, and missing sessions are not no-trade facts.

Conditional reconsideration requires aligned owner earnings and cash, clear current funding without assumed rescue, demonstrated incremental paid-product returns and a credible tradability record. A cheaper price alone cannot repair a cash-reliability or financing hold. This is research, not a buy/sell instruction or assurance of execution.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence is the issuer’s final prospectus, audited annual reports, May 2026 financial results, November 2025 half-year results, Maypostal notice, Junevoting outcome, Juneconversion board outcome and product-launch filing. Official exchange interoperability metadata/codebook verify exact identity, issued capital and lot, not trading liquidity. EquityPandit prices are explicitly secondary and incomplete. Tally/ClearTax/Intellect official materials supply product/industry context only; current Shopify documentation is not treated as a historical contract. Source URLs, exact downloaded byte hashes and locators accompany the evidence ledger.

The principal open questions are paid recurring revenue and cohorts, app-level cash development returns, maintenance versus growth engineering, current platform and ultimate-merchant concentration, owner-EPS/CFO/tax bridges, current deployable cash, actual subsidiary conversion and complete BSE liquidity. Missing information remains ND/NS. Company responses, resolved differences and contrary facts are retained; lack of a retrieved adverse order is not proof that none exists.

Forward growth, margins, receivable intensity, cash reserves, development budgets, normalized 25% cash tax, 13–18% illustrative capital cost, 8/12/16×exit multiples and rescue terms are analyst assumptions. No automatic tax credit, available financing, receivable release or completed conversion is asserted. Full historical and annual cash rows, stresses and calculation code are provided. Private analytical backups exclude original PDFs, OCR, HTML, images, shareholder lists and identifiers. They retain safe numerical inputs, derived analysis, references and hashes. Reproduction verifies calculations and internal consistency, not fresh original-source authenticity; that requires re-downloading cited originals and comparing their hashes.
